title_en: Tang Zhihua et al. (five persons) — corruption, duty encroachment, and bribery by enterprise personnel
keywords_en: criminal; embezzlement; occupational embezzlement; bribery of enterprise personnel; first instance; Intermediate People's Court; Shanghai; natural person; legal person; Criminal Law; whether adding procurement links constitutes embezzlement or occupational embezzlement; whether falsifying expenses constitutes embezzlement; whether accepting property constitutes bribery of enterprise personnel; adding procurement links; falsifying expenses; accepting property; bribery
full_text_en:
Tang Zhihua et al. (five persons) — embezzlement, occupational embezzlement, and bribery by enterprise personnel

Procuratorial Authority: First Branch of Shanghai Municipal People's Procuratorate.

Defendant: Tang Zhihua, male, 46 years old, former legal representative of Shanghai Baoqiang Industrial Co., Ltd., arrested on February 23, 2000.

Defense Counsel: Lü Shengqing, lawyer from Zheng Chuanben Law Firm.

Defense Counsel: Xu Wenbao, lawyer from Shanghai Kewei Law Firm.

Defendant: Shao Xianchu, male, 52 years old, former director of Shanghai Jinggong Machinery Electrical Appliance Factory, arrested on March 22, 2000.

Defense Counsel: Zhao Nengwen, lawyer from Shanghai Yishi Law Firm.

Defense Counsel: Du Aiwu, lawyer from Shanghai Huayuan Law Firm.

Defendant: Zhang Yong, male, 41 years old, former deputy director of Shanghai Jinggong Machinery Electrical Appliance Factory, arrested on July 19, 2000.

Defense Counsel: Huang Minggang, lawyer from Shanghai Liancheng Law Firm.

Defendant: Zhang Longhai, male, 48 years old, former director of Shanghai Third Printing Machinery Factory, arrested on July 12, 2000.

Defense Counsel: Zhai Jian and Yu Zengguo, lawyers from Shanghai Mingri Law Firm.

Defendant: Liu Kaikai, male, 55 years old, former deputy director of Shanghai Third Printing Machinery Factory, arrested on July 12, 2000.

Defense Counsel: Wang Xiangbao and Huang Donghong, lawyers from Zheng Chuanben Law Firm.

The case of defendants Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong for embezzlement, occupational embezzlement, and bribery by enterprise personnel was initiated by the First Branch of Shanghai Municipal People's Procuratorate to the Shanghai First Intermediate People's Court.

Indictment allegations:

Defendant Tang Zhihua conspired with defendant Zhang Longhai, who served as the director of Shanghai Third Printing Machinery Factory (hereinafter referred to as "Sanyin Factory"), to add an intermediate supply link for Sanyin Factory, embezzling over RMB 770,000 in excess payments made by Sanyin Factory, which were appropriated by Tang Zhihua. Tang Zhihua and Zhang Longhai also, together with defendant Liu Kaikai, who served as deputy director of Sanyin Factory, took advantage of their positions to fabricate various expenses, defrauding Sanyin Factory of over RMB 240,000 in public funds, which were appropriated by Tang Zhihua. The conduct of the three defendants violated Article 382 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Law) and constituted the crime of embezzlement.

Defendant Tang Zhihua conspired with defendants Shao Xianchu and Zhang Yong, who respectively served as director and deputy director of Shanghai Jinggong Machinery Electrical Appliance Factory (hereinafter referred to as "Jinggong Factory"), to add an intermediate supply link for Jinggong Factory, illegally taking possession of over RMB 2.6 million in excess payments made by Jinggong Factory, which were appropriated by Tang Zhihua. The conduct of the three defendants violated Article 271 of the Criminal Law and constituted the crime of occupational embezzlement.

Defendant Shao Xianchu, while serving as director of Jinggong Factory, took advantage of his position to accept bribes totaling RMB 24,800 from others. Shao Xianchu's conduct violated Article 163 of the Criminal Law and constituted the crime of bribery by enterprise personnel.

Defendants Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong surrendered themselves after committing the crimes and should be punished according to law.

To support the above allegations, the prosecutorial authority read out and presented in court the identity and position certificates of defendants Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong; testimony of witnesses who did not appear in court, including Zhang Shaoxiang, Yang Jian, Lü Chengji, Wu Youling, Tang Kai, Tu Jian, Liu Xueming, Wang Dejun, Ren Xuefeng, and Han Yumei; relevant purchase and sale invoices, payment certificates, receipt vouchers, audit and price appraisal conclusions; and the confessions made by Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong at the investigative authorities after their arrest. Additionally, witnesses Han Donghai and Chen Tingchun, and appraiser Chen Huaming were called to testify in court.

In response to the indictment, defendants Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong argued that the addition of the supply link was based on actual needs and was not a conspiracy; that Tang Zhihua's profits were not realized through resale at a markup to misappropriate enterprise funds, but primarily by lowering the sales prices from upstream suppliers. Therefore, the defendants had no criminal intent or conduct. Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, and Liu Kaikai further argued that the over RMB 240,000 paid by Sanyin Factory was incurred because Tang Zhihua had introduced Han Donghai to provide technical services to Sanyin Factory, and thus did not constitute embezzlement.

The defense counsels for each defendant also argued that Tang Zhihua's profits mainly came from price concessions granted by his upstream suppliers; that after Tang Zhihua introduced Han Donghai to provide technical services to Sanyin Factory, the factory was obliged to pay the technical service fee; and that Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong never received any benefits from Tang Zhihua's earnings, demonstrating that they had neither criminal purpose nor motive, and their conduct did not constitute a crime. The allegations that Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong conspired to commit the crimes of embezzlement and occupational embezzlement were based on unclear facts and insufficient evidence, and could not be established.

The defense counsel for Zhang Longhai further submitted that if Zhang Longhai's conduct were to be considered criminal, it could only constitute the crime of illegally seeking profits for relatives and friends under Article 166 of the Criminal Law. Considering that Zhang Longhai, during his tenure as executive deputy director and director of Sanyin Factory, had made significant efforts and contributions to the enterprise's production, operation, and market development, he should be exempted from punishment.

Defendant Shao Xianchu raised no objection to the facts of accepting bribes as charged in the indictment, but argued that he did not take advantage of his position and that the proceeds were used for business entertainment. Based on this, Shao Xianchu's defense counsel argued that Shao Xianchu accepted property from others for business entertainment purposes, and his conduct did not constitute the crime of bribery by enterprise personnel; the facts supporting this charge were unclear and the evidence insufficient.

Facts Found by Shanghai First Intermediate People's Court upon Trial:

I. Regarding the Crime of Embezzlement and the Crime of Occupational Embezzlement

Defendant Tang Zhihua was originally an employee of Shanghai Dongfang Papermaking Machinery Factory. After resigning in 1986, he engaged in individual transportation and furniture brokerage businesses. During this period, Tang Zhihua maintained a close relationship with Lu Zhongxin, former general manager of Shanghai Printing and Packaging Machinery Corporation (hereinafter referred to as "Yinbao Company"). Sanyin Factory was a state-owned enterprise subordinate to Yinbao Company. Defendants Zhang Longhai and Liu Kaikai were appointed by Yinbao Company as executive deputy director (presiding over work) and deputy director of the factory, respectively, in October 1996. Jinggong Factory was a collective enterprise supervised by Shanghai Ziguang Machinery Co., Ltd., a Sino-foreign joint venture of Yinbao Company. Defendants Shao Xianchu and Zhang Yong were appointed by the supervisory unit as director and deputy director of the factory, respectively, in December 1995.

In June 1995, defendant Tang Zhihua registered a private enterprise, Shanghai Baoqiang Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Baoqiang Company"), with himself as the legal representative, at Huangdu Town, Jiading District, Shanghai, and operated it jointly with his wife, Chen Tingchun. To make the company profitable, Tang Zhihua used his familiarity with Lu Zhongxin and others to exert influence over Yinbao Company and its subordinate enterprises.

After defendant Zhang Longhai became the executive deputy director of Sanyin Factory, he took advantage of his position in charge of the factory's overall work and procurement to conspire with defendant Tang Zhihua to instruct the procurement personnel of Sanyin Factory's Supply Department, when purchasing supporting parts such as electric motors and frequency converters, to have the suppliers — Shanghai Huasheng Electrical Equipment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Huasheng Company"), Shanghai Huaguang Digital Control Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Huaguang Company"), Shanghai Fuji Electrical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Fuji Company"), and Shanghai Pepperl+Fuchs Automation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Pepperl+Fuchs Company") — continue to supply directly to Sanyin Factory, but instead settle payments through Tang Zhihua's Baoqiang Company, which would then add a markup when settling with Sanyin Factory; Sanyin Factory would pay the货款 directly to Baoqiang Company. From January 1997 to December 1999, the above suppliers supplied goods worth a total of approximately RMB 1.881 million to Sanyin Factory, while Tang Zhihua, under the name of Baoqiang Company, settled payments for these goods to Sanyin Factory totaling approximately RMB 2.744 million (after deducting applicable taxes). According to the price appraisal conclusion of Shanghai Price Appraisal Office, Tang Zhihua's markup on reissued invoices amounted to approximately RMB 862,000, with an average markup of over 45% of the original price. After deducting possible sales discounts from the suppliers, Tang Zhihua and Zhang Longhai used the reissued invoices to cause Sanyin Factory to pay an excess of approximately RMB 777,000, which was appropriated by Tang Zhihua.

Between January and February 1997, defendant Tang Zhihua learned that Sanyin Factory was carrying out a technical renovation of electric motors and introduced Han Donghai, deputy general manager and engineer of Huaguang Company, to inspect the site. After arriving at Sanyin Factory, Han Donghai participated in the technical renovation of the electric motors alongside the factory's own technical personnel. Subsequently, because Sanyin Factory purchased and used Huaguang Company's motor products and accessories, neither Huaguang Company nor Han Donghai demanded payment for Han Donghai's participation in the technical renovation. Taking advantage of this opportunity, Tang Zhihua, on the pretext that he had introduced technical assistance that benefited Sanyin Factory, repeatedly requested defendants Zhang Longhai and Liu Kaikai to pay him an introduction fee. From February 1997 to mid-October 1999, Zhang Longhai and Liu Kaikai, knowing that Tang Zhihua was fabricating justifications for money, nevertheless took advantage of their positions to fabricate expenses under the names of engineering service fees, wall panel processing fees, and technical consultancy fees payable to Baoqiang Company, and on eight occasions paid a total of RMB 245,500 in public funds from Sanyin Factory to Tang Zhihua, who appropriated the entire sum.

Defendant Tang Zhihua, in order to intervene in the procurement of supporting parts such as frequency converters and programmable controllers for Jinggong Factory, conspired with defendants Shao Xianchu and Zhang Yong. Shao and Zhang, taking advantage of their positions in charge of and overseeing procurement for Jinggong Factory, secretly added an intermediate supply link, instructing the existing suppliers Huasheng Company and Huaguang Company to continue supplying directly to Jinggong Factory, but instead settle payments through Tang Zhihua's Baoqiang Company, which would then add a markup when settling with Jinggong Factory; Jinggong Factory would pay the货款 directly to Baoqiang Company. From December 1995 to December 1999, Huasheng Company and Huaguang Company supplied goods worth a total of approximately RMB 6.526 million to Jinggong Factory, while Tang Zhihua, under the name of Baoqiang Company, settled payments for these goods to Jinggong Factory totaling approximately RMB 9.678 million (after deducting applicable taxes). According to the price appraisal conclusion of Shanghai Price Appraisal Office, Tang Zhihua's markup on reissued invoices amounted to approximately RMB 3.151 million, with an average markup of over 48% of the original price. After deducting possible sales discounts from Huasheng Company and Huaguang Company, Tang Zhihua, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong used the reissued invoices to cause Jinggong Factory to pay an excess of approximately RMB 2.645 million, which was appropriated by Tang Zhihua.

In summary, defendant Tang Zhihua, through defendants Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong, embezzled and illegally took possession of a total of over RMB 3.667 million in funds from Sanyin Factory and Jinggong Factory. Tang Zhihua used a small portion of this money to purchase gifts for Zhang Yong or to provide meals and inducements to Shao Xianchu, Zhang Yong, Liu Kaikai, and others, and used the remainder to purchase a residential apartment and for bank deposits and securities trading. After the case came to light, some of the funds and goods at Tang Zhihua's disposal, as well as gifts he had given to Zhang Yong, were seized.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence:

(1) Evidence establishing the nature of the entities involved in the case and the identities of each defendant includes:

1. The business license, shareholder identity, and capital contribution certificates of Baoqiang Company; the testimony of Chen Tingchun, Tang Zhihua's wife; and Tang Zhihua's confessions, proving that Baoqiang Company was Tang Zhihua's private company with two shareholders: Tang Zhihua and his wife Chen Tingchun; that Baoqiang Company had no capital, operational personnel, operational capacity, or business premises; and that neither Tang Zhihua nor Chen Tingchun had any knowledge of the procurement and supply of relevant electromechanical products and accessories.

2. The enterprise legal person business license of Sanyin Factory, the "Cadre Resume Forms" filled in by Zhang Longhai and Liu Kaikai, the position certificates of Zhang Longhai and Liu Kaikai, and their confessions, proving that Sanyin Factory was a state-owned enterprise and that Zhang Longhai and Liu Kaikai, as the factory's director and deputy director, had the status of state functionaries.

3. The enterprise legal person business license of Jinggong Factory, the position certificates of Shao Xianchu and Zhang Yong, and their confessions, proving that Jinggong Factory was a collective enterprise and that Shao Xianchu and Zhang Yong were appointed as director and deputy director in December 1995, respectively in charge of and overseeing the factory's supply and sales work.

(2) Evidence establishing that Tang Zhihua and Zhang Longhai used the method of marking up reissued invoices to cause Sanyin Factory to pay an excess of approximately RMB 777,000 includes:

1. The supply invoices from Huasheng Company, Huaguang Company, Fuji Company, and Pepperl+Fuchs Company; the invoices issued by Baoqiang Company to Sanyin Factory; the loan advance receipts of Sanyin Factory approved by Zhang Longhai's signature; and the audit and price appraisal reports, confirming that Tang Zhihua and Zhang Longhai caused Sanyin Factory to pay an excess of approximately RMB 777,000 through markups on reissued invoices.

2. The initial invoices issued by Huasheng Company and other suppliers to Baoqiang Company, the initial invoices issued by Baoqiang Company to Sanyin Factory, and the initial payment vouchers from Sanyin Factory to Baoqiang Company confirm that Sanyin Factory not only paid first but also had over RMB 90,000 in货款 occupied by Baoqiang Company after deducting contemporaneous payments due.

3. Liu Xueming, an employee of Yinbao Company, testified: "Because Sanyin Factory was going to change its director, Zhang Longhai very much wanted the position. Later, word spread that Liu Kaikai might become director. Zhang Longhai then said to me, 'This must be Tang Zhihua helping Liu; Liu Kaikai and Tang Zhihua have a very good relationship.' So I took Zhang Longhai to Tang Zhihua's home. When Tang saw Zhang Longhai, he scolded Zhang, saying he 'didn't know the ropes.' I said some good words for Zhang on the side. Tang Zhihua later said to Zhang Longhai, 'From now on, you need to be more sensible. Anyway, I have this matter noted.' At that time, both Zhang and I got the impression that Tang Zhihua had a lot of influence in the printing and packaging industry."

Wu Youling, deputy section chief of Sanyin Factory's Supply Department, testified: "At the end of 1996, Zhang Shaoxiang of Huasheng Company took me to Tang Zhihua's home. Tang said to me that Liu Kaikai had just left and told me to procure accessories from his Baoqiang Company in the future, adding that Director Zhang Longhai would give me instructions on this matter. Two or three days later, Zhang Longhai called me to his office, where Tang Zhihua was also present. Zhang said that from then on, our factory's accessories would be handled by Tang Zhihua. He told me to discuss the specifics with Tang Zhihua. Later, Zhang said to me that Tang should make a 5% profit from our factory, and he wouldn't concern himself with anything else. All the actual quantities required, deliveries, and pickups for our factory were arranged directly by me with Huasheng, Pepperl+Fuchs, Fuji, and other units. These units issued invoices to Baoqiang Company, and Baoqiang Company merely bookkept and then issued invoices to our factory at a markup. Later, the prices charged by Baoqiang Company to our factory became higher and higher, with the markup far exceeding 5%. Zhang Longhai was aware of this, but he never asked me how much the markup actually was. I think he wanted to keep a way out for himself. Tang Zhihua often said to me that he had made Zhang Longhai the director, and that Zhang should now let him make money from the business. He said similar things in front of Zhang Longhai many times. Zhang Longhai repeatedly complained to me that Baoqiang Company's prices were high, but he never explicitly told me what to do afterward, and he continued to sign off on payments."

Zhang Shaoxiang, former financial supervisor of Huasheng Company, testified: "After getting to know Tang Zhihua, one day Shao Xianchu called to invite me to dinner. At the dinner table, there was also Liu Kaikai, the deputy director of Sanyin Factory. During the meal, Director Liu showed me a list of electrical appliances that Sanyin Factory intended to purchase. After looking at it, I said, 'These products are already being supplied to you, and the contact person is Wu Youling.' Tang then said to call Wu over. After dinner, we went to Tang's home. Liu Kaikai made a phone call, and I took the phone and asked Wu to come. Tang said to Wu that from then on, Sanyin Factory's business would be handled by his Baoqiang Company; Sanyin Factory could directly order electrical appliances from Huasheng, but the invoices had to go through Baoqiang Company."

Han Donghai, an employee of Huaguang Company, testified: "After my company established a business relationship with Jinggong Factory, Tang Zhihua said that Sanyin Factory had a batch of motors with quality problems and asked me to find a solution. I went there, and Sanyin Factory gradually replaced parts, all using my company's products. My company became a supplier to Sanyin Factory, with Tang Zhihua acting as an intermediary. In the actual dealings with Sanyin Factory, Tang had a very arrogant tone. He would scold Zhang Longhai and Liu Kaikai freely, and they had to do as he said. Tang knew nothing about motor prices; he would always ask me what the market price was. Then he would issue invoices to Sanyin Factory at very high prices. For example, we supplied Tang with a small cable worth about RMB 600, and Chen Tingchun invoiced Sanyin Factory at over RMB 1,000. The business clerk Wu Youling went to ask them about it, and Tang said to Wu, 'Regarding prices, you as a business clerk have no right to discuss this with me.' Baoqiang Company made money from Sanyin Factory; my company suffered no loss."

Tang Kai, general manager of Fuji Company, testified: "My company established a business relationship with Sanyin Factory in early 1996. After two or three transactions, Wu Youling told us that in the future, invoices should be issued to Baoqiang Company. After that, Wu would provide us with the product models and quantities, we would deliver the goods to Sanyin Factory, and hand the invoices to Wu Youling. He would then collect a check from Baoqiang Company and give it to us. To this day, we don't even know what kind of company Baoqiang is or who its boss is."

Tu Jian, an employee of Pepperl+Fuchs Company, testified: "Before Tang Zhihua, Sanyin Factory already had business dealings with Pepperl+Fuchs. At the end of 1996, I met Tang Zhihua for the first time. Tang said he had close ties with Yinbao Company, and that from then on he would place orders and pay, but the goods had to be delivered directly to the end user by us. I agreed. Tang proposed that for all customers in the printing and packaging industry that had previously had business dealings with my company, including those that would in the future, Baoqiang Company would act as the agent, and he asked us to grant him agency rights."

3. Witness Chen Tingchun testified: "All the business with Sanyin Factory was initially negotiated by Tang Zhihua. Huasheng, Fuji, and Pepperl+Fuchs were originally suppliers to Sanyin Factory, and Wu Youling introduced them to me. Generally, Wu would notify the suppliers of the required quantities, the suppliers would deliver directly to Sanyin Factory, and Wu would bring the invoices to my home. I would then reissue invoices to Sanyin Factory, and Sanyin Factory would make payment. Sometimes the货款 was also handed over to the suppliers through Wu. The prices were basically set by me."

4. Defendant Zhang Longhai, after his arrest, confessed: "In January 1996, I went to Tang Zhihua's home with Liu Xueming. Tang said he knew many leaders in the printing and packaging industry, and he spoke with a very arrogant tone. That summer, Tang called me over and proposed that I give him the procurement business for Sanyin Factory. I agreed, but I made it clear that he could only make a 5% profit from our factory. I thought, since he knew many leaders in the company, giving him the factory's procurement business would be beneficial to me. If I ran into trouble in the future, he could help me through the higher-ups. At the end of 1996, Tang Zhihua came to Sanyin Factory, and I called Wu Youling over, telling Tang to discuss directly with Wu. Afterward, I instructed Wu that from then on, the factory's procurement should be handled by Tang, allowing him to make a 5% profit in the middle. In fact, Tang Zhihua did make money from our factory. Because I considered that Tang had good relations with my superiors, I dared not sever the business relationship with him in order to keep my position. As a result, state assets suffered considerable losses."

Defendant Tang Zhihua's post-arrest confession: At the end of 1995, Liu Xueming accompanied Zhang Longhai to my home. Because the director of the Third Printing Factory was about to be transferred at that time, Zhang Longhai wanted to become the director and take charge. Both of them knew that I had a close relationship with the leaders of the Printing and Packaging Company. I agreed to put in a good word for Zhang with the company's general manager. At the beginning of 1996, Zhang Longhai was appointed as the Executive Deputy Director of the Third Printing Factory, fully in charge of its operations. In the second half of 1996, the business of the Third Printing Factory improved. I went to the factory to find Zhang Longhai and proposed that I would handle the supply of electrical appliances. Because when Zhang Longhai had previously asked me for help, he said that after he became the director and the factory's business improved, he would also let me make some money. So when I approached him this time, he agreed to my request on the spot, told me to contact Wu Youling, and said he would give specific instructions to Wu. Regardless of whether Zhang Longhai knew the truth, he should be grateful to me for helping him become the director. He asked for my help, and he got the position – that's a fact. In our dealings with the Third Printing Factory, we merely handled invoicing and transfers. Because the price markup later became too high, Wu Youling was dissatisfied. I said to Wu several times: "So what if I make money from your factory? Your director was also put in place by me; I made him director. As for the price issue, you go back and discuss it with Zhang." As expected, after Wu reported it to Zhang Longhai, there was no further action.

(3) Evidence establishing that Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, and Liu Kaikai embezzled RMB 245,500 from the Third Printing Factory by falsely listing various expenses includes:

1.  Audit and appraisal reports, and payment requisition forms signed or approved by Liu Kaikai and Zhang Longhai, confirming that the Third Printing Factory paid a total of RMB 245,500 in various service fees to Baoqiang Company; testimony from Ren Xuefeng and Han Yumei, staff of the Third Printing Factory's finance department, also confirming that the aforementioned amounts were paid in full to Baoqiang Company.

2.  Han Donghai, an employee of Huaguang Company, stated: He participated in the technical renovation of the Third Printing Factory, but he never negotiated with the Third Printing Factory, nor was he aware that the factory had paid RMB 245,500 to Baoqiang Company under the name of technical service fees.
    Wang Dejun, an employee of the Third Printing Factory, stated: The Third Printing Factory carried out a technical renovation, and Han Donghai came to participate and provide assistance. Because the factory would later use Huaguang's products, Han was responsible for helping the factory improve the quality of those products; therefore, it was impossible to pay Han Donghai technical service fees.

3.  Defendant Zhang Longhai's post-arrest confession: In early 1997, Tang Zhihua introduced Han Donghai to our factory to jointly study and solve the quality issue of automatic screen printing machines. After that, we used accessories supplied by Huaguang. In April 1997, Liu Kaikai said Tang Zhihua wanted to charge our factory a consulting fee. Liu then took out an invoice issued by Baoqiang Company for technical consulting fees and asked me to sign, which I did. The first time was RMB 20,000. Our factory paid technical consulting fees 7–8 times in total. Liu Kaikai brought the invoices for me to sign, totaling over RMB 200,000. Each time, Tang Zhihua had the invoice prepared in advance, and the amount was arbitrarily determined by him without any basis.
    Defendant Liu Kaikai's post-arrest confession: When I was transferred from Xinxiang Factory to the Third Printing Factory in 1993, I once asked Tang Zhihua for help. Tang said he had already spoken with Lu Zhongxin, the General Manager of the Printing and Packaging Company, and the decision was made, so I could rest assured. Afterwards, I successfully transferred into the Third Printing Factory. In early 1997, I told Tang that our factory's motors frequently needed repairs. Later, Tang introduced Han Donghai to help solve the problem, and our factory began using Han's company's products through Baoqiang Company as an intermediary. In February 1997, at Tang's home, I mentioned that the factory's machine sales were quite good. Tang then proposed that the Third Printing Factory take out some money. I said we could issue some invoices under the name of engineering services and get Zhang Longhai to agree. Later, Tang issued an invoice to me. After I got to work, I said to Zhang Longhai: "Tang Zhihua has sent an invoice asking for money." A few days later, Zhang Longhai told me to prepare and send a check, so I did. This engineering service fee had nothing to do with the motor renovation; it was my own idea, essentially taking money out of the factory to give to Tang Zhihua. From the first payment to the last, there were a total of eight times, with the total amount around RMB 230,000. Actually, Zhang Longhai and I knew from the beginning that transferring enterprise funds to Tang's Baoqiang Company under the guise of technical service fees was wrong. We both felt uneasy, worried about being held accountable in the future.
    Defendant Tang Zhihua's post-arrest confession: In early 1997, I learned that the Third Printing Factory had some motor problems, so I contacted Han Donghai to go to the factory for technical renovation. Later, at my home one time, Liu Kaikai said the factory was doing well, so I proposed getting some money for myself. Liu Kaikai suggested that the only way to get money was under the name of engineering service fees; I could issue an invoice, but it had to be approved by Zhang Longhai. Liu's remark reminded me; it was a good opportunity to ask the Third Printing Factory for money under the pretext of introducing Han Donghai. The next day, I called Zhang Longhai and said that I had introduced Han Donghai to renovate the 720 motor, and now that business was good, I wanted him to give me some money under the name of technical service fees. Zhang hesitated for a moment but agreed. I asked Liu to take the invoice back. Afterwards, I obtained several more sums of money from the Third Printing Factory by issuing invoices under technical service and similar names. In the second half of 1999, Zhang Longhai learned that the company's leaders were in trouble. He was very nervous at the time and told me to sign a supplementary agreement regarding the technical service fees. His meaning was that without an agreement, giving me money might cause problems. But at that time, I was busy dealing with the affairs of the Printing and Packaging Company's leaders and didn't take it to heart at all. I replied to Zhang that it was fine, and no agreement was signed.

4.  Witness Chen Tingchun's statement: Tang Zhihua once introduced Han Donghai to improve technology for the Third Printing Factory. Based on this fact, we had an excuse to ask the Third Printing Factory for money, and we indeed received a considerable amount. This occurred between March 1997 and October 1999, at irregular intervals. Whenever the Third Printing Factory was doing well, we would go collect some money, sometimes more, sometimes less. The largest amount was RMB 50,000, mostly between RMB 20,000 and RMB 30,000. Liu Kaikai instructed me to issue the invoices that way. Their purpose was that the factory could include the costs in its financial accounts. Tang Zhihua's and my purpose was to get the money; as for how the invoices were issued, we didn't care.

(4) Evidence establishing that Tang Zhihua, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong caused the Jinggong Factory to overpay RMB 2,645,000 by using the method of price markup and re-issuing invoices includes:

1.  Supply invoices from Huasheng Company and Huaguang Company, invoices issued by Baoqiang Company to the Jinggong Factory, receiving slips and payment vouchers signed or approved by Shao Xianchu and Zhang Yong respectively, check stubs signed by Tang Zhihua and Zhang Yong, audit reports, and price appraisal reports, confirming that Tang Zhihua, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong, through price markup and re-issuing of invoices, caused the Jinggong Factory to overpay a total of RMB 2,645,000.

2.  Lyu Chengji, a purchaser for the Jinggong Factory, stated: I was specifically responsible for the procurement of electrical items for our factory. Around 1994 to 1995, Shao Xianchu told me to stop purchasing frequency converters, saying someone from the Electromechanical Bureau wanted to sell them. After that, I stopped buying frequency converters, and Shao Xianchu took over the purchasing.
    Zhang Shaoxiang, former Finance Supervisor of Huasheng Company, stated: Our company had business dealings with the Jinggong Factory since 1992. Because the specifications and models of programmable controllers and frequency converters were complex and prices were high, it was always Shao Xianchu who came to our company to make purchases. At the end of 1995, Shao told me that from then on, invoices for goods sold to the Jinggong Factory should be issued to Baoqiang Company. From then on, Huasheng Company's sales invoices to the Jinggong Factory were issued to Baoqiang Company. Although Baoqiang Company stepped in, it was still Shao Xianchu who requested the goods from our company. According to Shao's request, I had the goods delivered directly to the Jinggong Factory's warehouse, where they were signed for. Then I sealed the invoices from our company to Baoqiang Company in an envelope and handed them to Shao Xianchu. Shao would then give me Baoqiang Company's payment check.
    Yang Jian, an employee of Huaguang Company, stated: Before 1996, our company supplied goods directly to the Jinggong Factory. Afterwards, Zhang Yong asked me to go to Tang Zhihua's home. Tang explicitly requested that our company's supplies to the Jinggong Factory be sold to the Jinggong Factory through Baoqiang Company as an intermediary, but the goods themselves were to be delivered directly by our company to the Jinggong Factory. I agreed. The price was based on our company's purchase cost plus a 3% profit, sold to Baoqiang Company. This continued until the end of 1999. After three years of contact, I believed that Tang Zhihua was merely using Baoqiang Company's VAT invoices for accounting purposes. He didn't have to exert any effort; he made money simply by re-issuing invoices.

3.  Defendant Zhang Yong's post-arrest confession: Tang Zhihua and I were former colleagues. In 1995, the factory I worked at was selling its land, and I was very anxious about my job transfer. Tang Zhihua helped me find the manager of Ziguang Company. After an interview, I was hired as the Deputy Director of the Jinggong Factory. I was very grateful to Tang Zhihua for this. Shao Xianchu got to know Tang Zhihua through me. When Tang Zhihua sold goods to the Jinggong Factory, he always required payment before delivery. Sometimes when he lacked funds to purchase goods, the Jinggong Factory even lent him money. Because we were purchasing from Tang Zhihua at inflated prices, to prevent the purchasers from finding out, I handled the transactions personally, as arranged by Shao Xianchu.
    Defendant Shao Xianchu's post-arrest confession: In October 1995, Zhang Yong introduced me to Tang Zhihua, and we had frequent contact afterwards. One evening at the end of 1995, Tang Zhihua called me to his home. He said he had no supply channels and asked me to introduce him to our factory's original suppliers. So I found Zhang Shaoxiang of Huasheng Company and explained that Baoqiang Company would first purchase from Huasheng and then sell to the Jinggong Factory. For the first batch of business, I handled it personally. I paid Baoqiang first, then Baoqiang settled with Huasheng, but the goods were delivered directly by Huasheng. Afterwards, I handed over all the specific operations to Zhang Yong. When I did business with Tang Zhihua, my inner thought was to befriend him and use his connections.
    Defendant Tang Zhihua's post-arrest confession: Zhang Yong was my former colleague. He often came to my home to play mahjong. Through Zhang Yong, I also got to know Shao Xianchu. Later, Shao frequently came to my home, and Zhang Yong often had meals at my place. I had boasted many times that I was the one who made Shao Xianchu the factory director. Shao and Zhang believed my words, so they wanted to curry favor with me and let me make money. Once, Shao came to my home and showed me some electrical appliances his factory needed, saying I could do this business with him. After looking at them, I said I didn't understand this business. Shao understood my meaning clearly and said it didn't matter if I didn't understand; the suppliers were the same ones they had always dealt with, and he would accompany me to make contact. Afterwards, with Shao's introduction, Huasheng Company would deliver goods to the Jinggong Factory, and Baoqiang Company would issue invoices to the Jinggong Factory for settlement. What we purchased from Huasheng Company was entirely based on the Jinggong Factory's requests. Through Zhang Yong's introduction, Huaguang Company, a subsidiary of the Printing and Packaging Company, also became one of my suppliers. In the business dealings with the Jinggong Factory, my company merely handled invoicing. At the time, I did realize this was irregular. The Jinggong Factory introduced their original suppliers to me, clearly allowing me to profit by making the factory pay more for goods that could have been purchased cheaper. I knew this money wasn't theirs personally; I was profiting from the Jinggong Factory's funds.

4.  Witness Chen Tingchun's statement: Baoqiang Company was a private enterprise owned by Tang Zhihua and me. The so-called registered capital of RMB 500,000 was false; no actual capital was contributed. Baoqiang Company had no other business premises; I just issued invoices and checks at home. After Baoqiang Company was established, Tang Zhihua often asked friends to give him business. Once, at my home, Tang and Shao Xianchu discussed doing business. Shao agreed that the frequency converters and programmable controllers for the Jinggong Factory would be purchased through Baoqiang Company. To be honest, Tang Zhihua and I knew nothing about this type of electrical equipment. So Shao often taught me how to issue invoices and how to add a markup to the price on Huasheng Company's invoices to Baoqiang Company before re-issuing invoices to the Jinggong Factory. Huasheng Company would deliver the goods directly to the Jinggong Factory and give the invoices to Shao Xianchu. Shao would then give me Huasheng Company's invoices, and I would re-issue invoices to the Jinggong Factory. Since these business connections were originally introduced to us by them, from the beginning to the end of the dealings with the Jinggong Factory, Shao and Zhang never raised any questions. Anyway, Baoqiang Company wasn't making money from their personal pockets but from the enterprise's funds, so they didn't care.

5.  As confirmed by the initial invoices from Huasheng Company to Baoqiang Company, the initial invoices from Baoqiang Company to the Jinggong Factory, and the initial payment vouchers from the Jinggong Factory to Baoqiang Company, the Jinggong Factory always paid for goods purchased from Baoqiang Company in advance. After deducting Baoqiang Company's contemporaneous payments to Huasheng Company, the Jinggong Factory still had several tens of thousands of yuan being occupied by Baoqiang Company.

II. Regarding the Crime of Acceptance of Bribes

From early 1998 to September 1999, the defendant Shao Xianchu, taking advantage of his position as the Director of the Jinggong Factory, repeatedly accepted property from business associates, including: RMB 21,500 in cash and electronic consumption cards worth RMB 1,800 from Gu Guoqiang, the private owner of Shanghai Jingshan Machinery Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd.; RMB 15,000 and an IC bus pass worth RMB 1,500 from Ding Huilai, the private owner of Zhejiang Yuyao Fangqiao Printing Machinery Parts Factory; and RMB 2,000 from Chen Jianhua, the contractor of Zhangjiagang Textile Auxiliary Machinery Factory, Jiangsu Province. The total amount of bribes accepted was RMB 24,800.

Evidence confirming the above facts includes:

1.  Gu Guoqiang's statement: In 1999, Shanghai Jingshan Machinery Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd. was commissioned by the Jinggong Factory to process products, with a business volume of RMB 1.5 million. During this period, I gave Shao Xianchu RMB 8,000 in cash and 24 electronic consumption cards, each worth RMB 100.

2.  Ding Huilai's statement: Regarding the processing of products for the Jinggong Factory by my factory, from early 1998 to autumn 1999, I gave Shao Xianchu a total of RMB 12,500 and three bus passes, each worth RMB 500. In January 2000, Shao learned that my son was getting married and gave me RMB 1,000 as a gift. In past interactions, I had also given him two bottles of liquor.

3.  Chen Jianhua's statement: My factory produced products for the Jinggong Factory under an outsourcing arrangement. In September 1999, after dinner in Kunshan, Shao Xianchu took a woman into a room. After waiting outside the alley for over an hour, Shao and the woman came out. Shao told me to take out RMB 2,000, so I gave the RMB 2,000 to Shao Xianchu.

4.  Statement of Sun Xiaoqi, an unemployed young woman: I worked as a hostess at a restaurant in Kunshan. After getting acquainted with Shao Xianchu, Shao came to Kunshan to see me more than ten times. Once, after I had sexual relations with Shao Xianchu in Kunshan, Shao called that person from Zhangjiagang to come over, and that person gave me RMB 2,000, saying it was a meeting gift.

5.  Confession of the defendant Shao Xianchu: I received RMB 8,000 from Gu Guoqiang and 18 electronic consumption cards from Hualian Supermarket, each worth RMB 100. Gu hoped I would help introduce business and gave these as expense money. I received RMB 12,500 and three bus passes worth RMB 1,500 from Ding Huilai. When Ding Huilai's son got married, I gave RMB 1,000 as a gift. As for Chen Jianhua's RMB 2,000, Chen said it was a meeting gift for Sun Xiaoqi, and Sun accepted it.

All the above evidence has been examined and cross-examined during the trial and can serve as the basis for determining the facts of this case.

It is also found that the defendants Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong all confessed their problems to the disciplinary inspection authorities before the investigative authorities took compulsory measures against them.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court holds:

Article 271 of the Criminal Law stipulates: "Any employee of a company, enterprise, or other unit who, taking advantage of his position, illegally takes possession of the property of his own unit for himself, if the amount is relatively large, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention; if the amount is huge, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years, and may also be sentenced to confiscation of property." "Any person who is engaged in public service in a State-owned company, enterprise, or other State-owned unit or who is assigned by a State-owned company, enterprise, or other State-owned unit to a non-State-owned company, enterprise, or other unit to engage in public service and commits the act prescribed in the preceding paragraph shall be convicted and punished according to the provisions of Articles 382 and 383 of this Law." Article 382 stipulates: "Any State functionary who, taking advantage of his position, embezzles, misappropriates, obtains by deception, or illegally takes possession of public property by other means shall be guilty of embezzlement." "Any person who is entrusted by a State organ, State-owned company, enterprise, institution, or people's organization to manage and operate State-owned property and, taking advantage of his position, embezzles, misappropriates, obtains by deception, or illegally takes possession of the State-owned property by other means shall be deemed to have committed embezzlement." "Any person who colludes with the persons mentioned in the preceding two paragraphs to engage in embezzlement shall be dealt with as an accomplice in the crime of embezzlement." Article 383 stipulates: "Any person who commits the crime of embezzlement shall be punished according to the seriousness of the circumstances and in accordance with the following provisions: (1) Where the amount of individual embezzlement is not less than RMB 100,000, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years or life imprisonment, and may also be sentenced to confiscation of property; where the circumstances are especially serious, he shall be sentenced to death and also to confiscation of property. (2) Where the amount of individual embezzlement is not less than RMB 50,000 but less than RMB 100,000, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 5 years, and may also be sentenced to confiscation of property; where the circumstances are especially serious, he shall be sentenced to life imprisonment and also to confiscation of property. (3) Where the amount of individual embezzlement is not less than RMB 5,000 but less than RMB 50,000, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 1 year but not more than 7 years; where the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 7 years but not more than 10 years. Where the amount of individual embezzlement is not less than RMB 5,000 but less than RMB 10,000, and the offender shows repentance after committing the crime and actively makes restitution, the punishment may be mitigated or a criminal penalty may be exempted, and his unit or the competent authority at a higher level shall give him administrative sanctions. (4) Where the amount of individual embezzlement is less than RMB 5,000, but the circumstances are relatively serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 2 years or criminal detention; where the circumstances are relatively minor, his unit or the competent authority at a higher level shall give him administrative sanctions as it deems fit." "Where multiple acts of embezzlement have not been dealt with, punishment shall be imposed according to the accumulated amount of embezzlement."

The Supreme People's Court, in Article 1 of the "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Joint Crimes of Embezzlement and Job Encroachment" (Fa Shi [2000] No. 15), stipulates: "Where a person conspires with a State functionary and uses the State functionary's position to jointly embezzle, misappropriate, obtain by deception, or illegally take possession of public property by other means, he shall be punished as an accomplice in the crime of embezzlement." Article 2 stipulates: "Where a person conspires with an employee of a company, enterprise, or other unit and uses the employee's position to jointly illegally take possession of the property of that unit for himself, if the amount is relatively large, he shall be punished as an accomplice in the crime of job encroachment."

The Third Printing Factory is a State-owned enterprise subordinate to the Printing and Packaging Company; its enterprise property is State-owned property. The defendants Zhang Longhai and Liu Kaikai are State functionaries working in this enterprise. The Jinggong Factory is a collectively-owned enterprise subordinate to a joint venture between the Printing and Packaging Company and a foreign party; its enterprise property is collectively owned. The defendants Shao Xianchu and Zhang Yong are employees of this collectively-owned enterprise. The defendant Tang Zhihua does not work for the victim units, the Third Printing Factory or the Jinggong Factory. He is neither a State functionary nor an employee of a collectively-owned enterprise. However, he used his relationships and influence within the Printing and Packaging Company to draw in and direct Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong to act for him, using their official positions to transfer RMB 3,667,000 in funds—which these two factories could have avoided spending—to his privately-established company, which had neither capital nor operational resources or capabilities, thereby embezzling and misappropriating them. In accordance with the aforementioned laws and judicial interpretations, Tang Zhihua and Zhang Longhai, by re-issuing invoices with a price markup, embezzled RMB 777,000 of State-owned property from the Third Printing Factory; Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, and Liu Kaikai, by falsely listing expenses, defrauded RMB 245,500 of State-owned property from the Third Printing Factory; their acts constitute the crime of embezzlement. Tang Zhihua, together with Shao Xianchu and Zhang Yong, by re-issuing invoices with a price markup, misappropriated RMB 2,645,000 of property from the Jinggong Factory; their acts constitute the crime of job encroachment. They shall all be punished according to law.

The audit conclusion and price appraisal, after taking into account the suppliers’ contemporaneous supply prices and market price indices, deducted the suppliers’ possible profit concessions, and determined that the defendant Tang Zhihua embezzled over RMB 777,000 from the Third Printing Factory and over RMB 2,645,000 from the Jinggong Factory, which were respectively over RMB 85,000 and over RMB 506,000 less than the actual payments received by Tang Zhihua based on the invoices he issued. Even so, Tang Zhihua's average markup rate exceeded 40%. Witnesses Yang Jian and Han Donghai confirmed that the price Hua Guang Company gave to Baoqiang Company was 3% above their purchase price; witness Tang Kai confirmed that the price Fuji Company gave to Baoqiang Company was 5% above their purchase price; witness Zhang Shaoxiang confirmed that the price Huasheng Company gave to Baoqiang Company was 5% above their purchase price. The price levels these companies gave to Baoqiang Company were only 3% to 5% lower than the prices they originally supplied to the Third Printing Factory and Jinggong Factory or the market prices at the time. Witness Han Donghai and others confirmed that in the above transactions, the suppliers suffered no losses. Witness testimony also confirmed that, apart from the markup and re-invoicing, Tang Zhihua did not even perform tasks such as delivering goods to the Third Printing Factory and Jinggong Factory. These circumstances indicate that the over RMB 3,422,000 obtained by Tang Zhihua through re-invoicing at a markup was the additional payment made by the Third Printing Factory and Jinggong Factory due to the artificially inflated supply chain link. The opinions of the defendants and their defense counsels that the money Tang Zhihua obtained was mainly derived from supplier profit concessions are inconsistent with the facts and are not adopted.

Article 13 of the Criminal Law stipulates: "All acts that endanger national sovereignty, territorial integrity and security, split the state, subvert the people's democratic dictatorship and overthrow the socialist system, disrupt social and economic order, infringe upon state-owned property or property collectively owned by the working masses, infringe upon citizens' privately owned property, infringe upon citizens' personal rights, democratic rights and other rights, and other acts that endanger society, which are subject to criminal punishment according to law, are crimes. However, if the circumstances are obviously minor and the harm is not great, they are not considered crimes." The defendant Tang Zhihua, knowing that the Baoqiang Company he established had no capital, no goods, resources, or operational capacity, used his influence and connections in the printing and packaging industry to recruit and instruct the defendants Zhang Longhai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong, taking advantage of their official positions, to insert his private company into the normal supply chain between the Third Printing Factory and Jinggong Factory and their original suppliers. By means of invoice markup and re-issuance, he appropriated state-owned and collectively-owned property for himself. This act undoubtedly infringed upon state-owned and collectively-owned property and was an act harmful to society subject to criminal punishment according to law.

Article 25 of the Criminal Law provides: "A joint crime refers to an intentional crime committed by two or more persons jointly." Persons participating in a joint intentional crime share the same criminal purpose. The criminal purpose of each defendant in this case is clear: to convert the state-owned and collectively-owned property of the Third Printing Factory and Jinggong Factory into the private property of defendant Tang Zhihua. The reason Tang Zhihua was able to extract huge sums of money from the Third Printing Factory and Jinggong Factory without any legitimate business or agency relationship was inseparable from the active cooperation of defendants Zhang Longhai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong, who utilized their respective official positions. Each defendant, when carrying out their respective acts, knew that they would infringe upon the lawful ownership of state-owned and collectively-owned property, but all desired to achieve this goal. Therefore, their acts constituted a joint intentional crime.

In a joint intentional crime, although each actor carries out harmful acts against society to achieve the same criminal purpose, the criminal motives that drive each actor to commit such harmful acts may differ. Different criminal motives do not affect the constitution of the crime. In this case, defendant Tang Zhihua carried out harmful acts driven by greed, whereas defendants Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong conspired with Tang Zhihua either out of gratitude for Tang Zhihua's past favors or to seek Tang Zhihua's help in securing positions for themselves. Each of them used their respective official positions to carry out harmful acts in order to achieve the criminal purpose of transferring the state-owned and collectively-owned property under their management and control to Tang Zhihua's private ownership. In this joint crime aimed at achieving that criminal purpose, the criminal acts of Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong — privately adding supply chain links and falsifying various expenses by taking advantage of their respective official positions — were indispensable components.

In a joint intentional crime aimed at property infringement, it is not excluded that individual actors may not participate in the division of spoils. The key to determining whether such a crime is constituted is not whether the actor obtained or how much spoils the actor obtained through committing the crime, but rather whether the property relations protected by the Criminal Law have been infringed upon and the degree of such infringement. It is a fact that defendants Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong did not share in the illicit proceeds from the joint crime. They and their defense counsels argue that this proves they had neither criminal purpose nor criminal motive and therefore did not constitute a crime. Failure to share spoils does not affect the determination of guilt; it can only be considered as a discretionary circumstance for sentencing. This defense argument cannot stand.

Article 166, item (2) of the Criminal Law stipulates that an employee of a state-owned company, enterprise, or institution who, by taking advantage of his position, "purchases commodities from a unit managed by his relatives or friends at a price manifestly higher than the market price, or sells commodities to a unit managed by his relatives or friends at a price manifestly lower than the market price" constitutes the crime of illegally seeking profits for relatives and friends. In this case, Baoqiang Company had neither capital nor operational capacity, had never actually conducted any legitimate purchase or sale of electrical goods, and was not itself a lawfully managed unit. The purpose of defendant Tang Zhihua in establishing Baoqiang Company was not to participate in market operations but to extract funds from state-owned and collectively-owned enterprises. Moreover, Tang Zhihua was not a relative or friend for whom defendant Zhang Longhai voluntarily sought profits. Zhang Longhai handed over the public funds of the Third Printing Factory to Tang Zhihua for possession out of a motive to retain his own position. Therefore, Zhang Longhai's conduct does not constitute the crime of illegally seeking profits for relatives and friends.

During his tenure as Deputy Executive Director and later Director of the Third Printing Factory, defendant Zhang Longhai did make efforts and contribute positively to the enterprise's production, operation, and market development. At the same time, however, Zhang Longhai, for personal gain, cooperated with defendant Tang Zhihua to embezzle the huge amount of state-owned assets managed by the Third Printing Factory. As a state functionary and a leading cadre of a state-owned enterprise, it was his duty to abide by laws and regulations and work diligently. Past merits and achievements can neither conceal illegal and criminal acts nor become grounds or reasons for exempting criminal liability. Anyone, regardless of how great their merits or contributions, is subject to criminal punishment if they violate criminal law. This is where the fairness of socialist justice lies. The defense argument of Zhang Longhai's counsel that Zhang Longhai's conduct constituted the crime of illegally seeking profits for relatives and friends and that, based on his past performance, he should be exempted from criminal liability, is not adopted.

Apart from accepting bribes totaling over RMB 24,800 from Gu Guoqiang, Ding Huilai, and Chen Jianhua, defendant Shao Xianchu also received cash of RMB 20,000 from Ding Huilai under the name of entertainment expenses, among others. This RMB 20,000 was placed in Shao Xianchu's private petty cash fund and used for business entertainment expenses; it was not recognized as criminal conduct in this case. Shao Xianchu and his defense counsel confuse the bribes Shao Xianchu accepted with the RMB 20,000 cash Shao Xianchu received from Ding Huilai, arguing that these funds were used for business entertainment and did not constitute the crime of bribery by an enterprise employee. This argument lacks factual basis and is not adopted.

In summary, the acts of defendants Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong respectively constitute the crimes of embezzlement, misappropriation of property by an enterprise employee, and bribery by an enterprise employee. They should all be punished according to law. The criminal acts of Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong severely disrupted the social and economic order. In accordance with Article 56 of the Criminal Law, deprivation of political rights may be imposed as a supplementary punishment. Tang Zhihua and Shao Xianchu each committed multiple crimes; in accordance with Article 69 of the Criminal Law, they shall be subject to combined punishment for multiple crimes. Tang Zhihua embezzled over RMB 1,000,000 of state-owned property, and should have been severely punished under Article 383, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Criminal Law. However, considering that the crime of embezzlement is generally constituted only by state functionaries, and the Criminal Law imposes heavy penalties for embezzlement based on the principle of heavier punishment for crimes committed by state functionaries, while Tang Zhihua is not a state functionary and committed this crime only with the cooperation of state functionaries, Tang Zhihua's crime of embezzlement may be given a lighter punishment within the statutory sentencing range. Although Shao Xianchu, Zhang Yong, Zhang Longhai, and Liu Kaikai participated in the joint crime, they did not share specific illicit proceeds and confessed their criminal conduct truthfully to the disciplinary inspection authorities before compulsory measures were taken by the investigative authorities. This should be regarded as voluntary surrender. In accordance with Article 67, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, Shao Xianchu and Zhang Yong may be given lighter punishment, and Zhang Longhai and Liu Kaikai may be given mitigated punishment. In accordance with Article 64 of the Criminal Law, all property obtained illegally by criminals shall be recovered or ordered to be returned or compensated. Accordingly, on February 22, 2001, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court ruled as follows:

1. Defendant Tang Zhihua is convicted of the crime of misappropriation of property by an enterprise employee and sentenced to 13 years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for 3 years, and confiscation of property in the amount of RMB 1,000,000; he is convicted of the crime of embezzlement and sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for 4 years, and confiscation of property in the amount of RMB 500,000; the combined sentence is 20 years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for 5 years, and confiscation of property in the amount of RMB 1,500,000.

2. Defendant Shao Xianchu is convicted of the crime of misappropriation of property by an enterprise employee and sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for 3 years; he is convicted of the crime of bribery by an enterprise employee and sentenced to 1 year's imprisonment; the combined sentence is 11 years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for 3 years.

3. Defendant Zhang Yong is convicted of the crime of misappropriation of property by an enterprise employee and sentenced to 9 years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for 2 years.

4. Defendant Zhang Longhai is convicted of the crime of embezzlement and sentenced to 8 years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for 1 year.

5. Defendant Liu Kaikai is convicted of the crime of embezzlement and sentenced to 5 years' imprisonment.

6. All property obtained by defendant Tang Zhihua through embezzlement and misappropriation shall be recovered; any shortfall shall be ordered to be returned or compensated. The illegal gains of defendants Shao Xianchu and Zhang Yong shall be recovered.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, defendants Tang Zhihua, Shao Xianchu, Zhang Yong, and Liu Kaikai, dissatisfied, filed appeals, still arguing that Baoqiang Company's profits came from supplier profit concessions, that the Third Printing Factory should have paid technical service fees, and that their conduct did not constitute a crime.

After trial in the second instance, the Shanghai High People's Court held: The appellant Tang Zhihua, in collusion with the defendant at first instance Zhang Longhai, appellant Liu Kaikai, and other employees of state-owned enterprises, and in collusion with appellants Shao Xianchu, Zhang Yong, and other employees of collective enterprises, took advantage of the official positions of Zhang Longhai, Liu Kaikai, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong as directors and deputy directors of state-owned and collective enterprises, causing Tang Zhihua to take possession of the purchase funds and other public funds of the state-owned and collective enterprises. The acts of Tang Zhihua, Zhang Longhai, and Liu Kaikai constitute the crime of embezzlement; the acts of Tang Zhihua, Shao Xianchu, and Zhang Yong constitute the crime of misappropriation of property by an enterprise employee. Shao Xianchu, taking advantage of his official position, accepted bribes worth RMB 24,800 from others, and his conduct also constitutes the crime of bribery by an enterprise employee. They should all be punished according to law. The appeal grounds of the four appellants are inconsistent with the facts found and are not adopted. The facts found in the first instance judgment are clear, the evidence is conclusive, the application of law is correct, the sentencing is appropriate, and the trial procedure is lawful; it should be affirmed. Accordingly, on May 8, 2001, the Shanghai High People's Court ruled:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.
